title: Decision to Refuse Entry to Foreign Religious Preachers
what_it_is: Decision to Refuse Entry to Foreign Religious Preachers

sections.label: Miscellaneous Work Pass for sensitive talks
sections.summary: Foreigners giving talks on religion, race or politics in Singapore must obtain a Miscellaneous Work Pass from the Ministry of Manpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In this context, the foreigner who wants to deliver a talk in Singapore, if the talk is related to religion, race or politics, he has to obtain a Miscellaneous Work Pass (MWP) from the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) because the issues are sensitive.

sections.label: Barring foreigners with radical antecedents
sections.summary: Foreigners with antecedents of radical preaching, violence or intolerant teachings are not allowed in, regardless of where comments were made or their following size.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: From a security perspective, one of the principles is that a foreigner should not have antecedents of radical preaching and teachings.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For example, if he has advocated violence or promoted segregationist, intolerant teachings that are inimical to our multiracial, multi-religious society, he will not be allowed in.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is not material whether the previous comments were made in relation to Singapore or whether they intend to touch on these issues when they speak here.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If they hold views that are inappropriate or unacceptable in our context, then it is not in our national interest to give them a platform in Singapore, whether to propagate their teachings or to build up their followings.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is also not material to consider how large their following is in Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore's religiously diverse society
sections.summary: Singapore encourages different faiths to carry on and is ranked one of the most religiously diverse societies in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Within Singapore, we are very clear on the framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We encourage the different faiths to carry on, you have seen the consequences, we are ranked one of the most religiously diverse societies in the world.

sections.label: Conservative approach to foreign preachers
sections.summary: Under the Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act framework, Singapore takes a conservative approach to foreign preachers, considering who brings them in and their past sayings.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act has a framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But essentially, if I were to identify one principle, do not do harm unto others, do not advocate violence, do not put down somebody else's religion.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That, I think, has seen us being an oasis of religious peace in a world that is highly troubled.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, when we look at foreign preachers, we would have to look at who is bringing them in, we will have to talk to them, and we will have to look at the context of their sayings.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But on the whole, we take a fairly conservative approach in that whatever you have said elsewhere, if those represent your viewpoints, like what I just said, if someone calls Allah a false God and then he wants to come into Singapore and say, "Well, you know, that was in a different context", I think, nevertheless, it runs the serious risk of people following such a preacher, and then they go on to look at what else he has said elsewhere and the context is not always apparent to people to be understood.
